suggestion: Unblock the nflverse release CDN (or vendor the injuries/depth_charts/snap_counts releases into this repo).
evidence: FLAG-01: 5 of 6 planned datasets came back unreachable; only git-hosted files worked.
cost: Low (infra). One allowlist entry or a scheduled mirror job.
risk: Low. Data is MIT-licensed open data.

suggestion: Freeze the gate thresholds in a signed config file before the next research cycle, and version it.
evidence: OQ-03 and OQ-10 are unanswered; the current defaults are the agent's, not the owner's.

suggestion: Treat every ROI as 'vs the close' and publish the implied half-edge haircut next to it.
evidence: Only closing prices are available for the full sample (OQ-01). A model-vs-close gap of X is worth at most X/2 in practice.
risk: None. It only makes the reported numbers more conservative.

suggestion: Backfill 2026 weeks 1-9 injury reports, then re-run the availability model on a full season before trusting it.
evidence: Availability model currently has 388 team-weeks, all 2025; the 2026 signal has n = 1 week.
cost: Medium. ~3,000 rows, or free once SG-01 lands.
missing: SG-01 or an authorisation to transcribe.

suggestion: Adopt a depth-order source with a timestamp, and only then build the 2nd/3rd/4th-string model.
evidence: Official roster pages carry no depth order (S06). nflverse depth_charts is blocked (D07).
risk: High if skipped: any depth claim without a timestamp is unfalsifiable.

suggestion: Do not build prop-combo pricing until a prop line/result dataset exists; keep the team-level correlation engine as the proxy.
evidence: data/correlations.csv measures same-game team correlations only. Player props are unmeasured (OQ-08).
risk: High: shipping prop combos on a team-level proxy would be a fabricated edge.

suggestion: Keep the 'zero strategies approved' headline prominent; do not soften it.
evidence: 0 of 15 variants passed all 7 gates. The control (bet every home team) returned -5.2% ROI, which is the vig, as expected.

suggestion: Prioritise building an independent line from non-result data (pace, EPA, injuries) before adding more price-based variants.
evidence: Every price-based variant (Elo vs close, prob gap) returned |ROI| < 3.5% and failed significance. The information is already in the close.
risk: Medium: result-history Elo is already known to underperform the market.
missing: Play-by-play and charting data (reachable, but large).

suggestion: Do not add parlays to the reward board on current evidence.
evidence: A 2-leg -110 parlay is -8.9% EV, 3-leg -13.0%, 4-leg -17.0% (data/parlay_economics.csv). Measured correlation does not flip the sign.
missing: Only revisit if a per-SGP correlation edge is proven.

suggestion: Publish the rejected list, not just the approved list, and keep the search count in the repo.
evidence: G6 (Bonferroni) is only meaningful if the number of searched variants is public. It currently is (15).

suggestion: Add a per-row 'verified at' timestamp and a build-failing link checker to every future data drop.
evidence: scripts/verify_site.py already fails the build on a table row without a source link; extend it to check HTTP status on every source.
risk: Low: link rot will cause occasional build failures by design.

suggestion: Investigate WIND15_UNDER properly rather than promoting it.
evidence: Best raw candidate: 425 bets, 55.1% hit, +7.2% ROI, p = 0.063 — fails G3 (p < 0.05) and G6 (p < 0.0033). OOS ROI +5.7%.
cost: Medium. Needs a wind forecaster and an opening-line feed.
risk: High. At p = 0.063 across 15 searches, this is exactly what noise looks like.
missing: Opening lines and forecast-time wind, not post-game measured wind.
